:::{#exr-identity-product-practice}
#### Multiplying by an identity matrix

@thm-identity says that an [identity matrix](#def-identity-matrix) of the right size leaves a [matrix](#def-matrix) unchanged under [matrix multiplication](#def-matrix-mult),
just as multiplying a number by $1$ leaves it unchanged.
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Compute $\matr{I}_2 \matr{A}$ entry by entry, from the definition of matrix multiplication.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Entry $(i, j)$ of $\matr{I}_2 \matr{A}$ is the [dot product](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-dot-product) of the $i$th [row of $\matr{I}_2$](#def-matrix-row) with the $j$th [column of $\matr{A}$](#def-matrix-column),
as in @exm-dot-product-matmul.

:::
